title: Pipeline tilemap binding prototype notes
content:
Notes to self: prototype idea for a compact runtime primitive I'm calling 'tilemap binding'.

Motivation:
- Observed high variance in per-token latency when KD-cache misses + cold KV for multi-turn sessions.
- We already do prefix caching at request-level; want a lightweight composable way to:
  1) break request context into reusable 'tiles' (short spans of tokenized context + provenance)
  2) bind tiles to session IDs and runtime lanes for fast lookup and prewarm
  3) let routing/ingress operate on tile identity (cheap hashes) instead of full context payloads

High-level primitive:
- Tile: immutable chunk: {tile_id, model_family, token_span_start, token_span_end, compact-hash, meta-tags} (meta includes user-sanity, source, creation_ts)
- Tilemap: ordered list of tiles representing a session window (sliding). Stored either in tenant-scoped cache or as session artifact in S3-like cold store.
- Binding: ephemeral mapping of (session_id -> tilemap + binding_metadata) pinned to an ingress lane / runtime shard for fast KV/attachment.

Goals / properties:
- Cheap identity: tile_id must be stable and short (8-12 chars base62) and derive from compact-hash to avoid collisions in practice.
- Incremental update: allow append/trim operations without rehashing whole map.
- Prefetch hooks: classifiers (access pattern + cost model) suggest next tiles to prefetch into runtime memory.
- Eviction model: keep recently used tiles pinned per-SLO; cheap rehydrate path if evicted.

Example API shapes (sketch - keep minimal):
- Create/Append tile (HTTP POST)
  POST /v1/tiles
  payload: {"session_id":"s123", "model":"vicuna-16b", "tokens":"...base64...", "provenance":"client-slice-1", "tags":["user-note"]} 
  response: {"tile_id":"t_8k3a9b", "compact_hash":"c_39f2"}

- Bind tilemap to session: POST /v1/session-bindings
  payload: {"session_id":"s123", "tiles": ["t_8k3a9b","t_1x7zq"], "pin_ttl_sec": 300, "prefetch": true}
  response: {"binding_id":"b_44g7","pinned_at":"..."}

- Resolve tilemap: GET /v1/session-bindings?s=session_id or binding_id -> returns tile descriptors + local cache status

Config sketch (YAML-like proto for runtime):
- tilemap:
    max_tiles_per_session: 64
    max_tile_bytes: 8192
    pin_ttl_sec_default: 120
    prefetch_budget_tokens: 1024
    eviction_policy: LRU+freq_weight
    compact_hash_algo: cityhash64
    allow_cross_model_tiles: false  # for now, restrict tiles to same model family

Runtime binding model (state machine ASCII):
  [Ingress] --create_tile--> [Tile Store] --append--> [Tilemap] --bind--> [Shard] --pin--> [Memory]
     |                                                                     ^
     +--request-resolve--> [Resolve svc] --if-miss-> fetch-from-[Cold-store]+rebuild

Prefetch / prediction pipeline (rough):
- Feature extractor: request headers + session meta + tile access histogram -> feature vector
- Prefetch predictor (lightweight): logistic reg -> score per candidate tile
- Prefetch queue: prioritized by score/cost; budget gating by pin_ttl and shard budget

Telemetry/events to emit (minimal):
- tile.create (tile_id, size_bytes, model, session_id?)
- tile.bind (binding_id, shard, pin_ttl_sec)
- tile.prefetch.request (candidate_count, budget_tokens)
- tile.resolve.hit/miss (latency_ms, src:memory|disk|cold)

Example flows (user scenario):
- Chat session: client sends message; ingress tokenizes and asks for session binding.
- If binding exists and tilemap is pinned -> fast KV lookup returns prefixes -> runtime reuses kv cache -> generation proceeds with <1ms tile lookup overhead.
- If binding exists but pin stale -> Resolve svc returns tile list + missing tiles; prefetch kickstarts; respond with progressive hydration (stream placeholder tokens until prefetch completes).

Edge cases / constraints:
- Cross-tenant collisions: ensure compact_hash + tile_id namespacing using tenant prefix.
- Privacy: tiles may contain PII; need optional client-side redaction flag -> tile stored encrypted with tenant KMS key.
- Model variant changes: revocation / invalidation when model version is rolled out. Tiles signed with model_version. On mismatch, treat as miss.
- Reconstruct cost vs storage: small tiles increase metadata overhead. Tune max_tile_bytes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to handle function/tool calling outputs as tiles? (structured objects vs raw text tokens)
- Should we expose batch-append API used by frontends to bundle multiple messages into tiles? (likely yes for perf)
- Backpressure: when prefetch budget exhausted, fall back to 'best-effort streaming' or deny prefetch? design policy DSL?
- GC semantics when session is closed but tiles still hot due to other sessions referencing them. Need ref counting or TTL-chaining.

Quick benchmark plan:
- Synthetic workload: 10k sessions, median turns 8, token distribution skewed (long tail). Measure 95th lat before/after pinning with tilemap.
- Cost model: estimate extra storage per session vs token cost saved via KV reuse.

Notes to self: keep prototype local to a single model family first (gpt-like), then generalize. Start with in-memory shard + backing S3 for cold store. Keep API minimal: create tile, bind, resolve. Iterate on prefetch predictor later.

Next steps:
- Spike: implement a small Go service that accepts POST /v1/tiles and stores tile metadata in Redis + blob in MinIO. Endpoint to bind and resolve. Hook a tiny predictor (logistic) as separate process.
- Doc: move cleaned draft into shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/tilemap-spec.md when prototype shows >10% p95 improvement.
- Chat with privacy team re: encryption flags + tagging for PII.

Random scribbles: compact-hash length tradeoffs: 36-bit hash (base62 ~6 chars) seems collision-y; prefer 64-bit but encoded into 11 base62 chars -> slightly longer but safer.

References: link to CONFLUENCE-1234 for earlier cache experiments; PR GITHUB-PR-4821 had some preliminary pinning logic.

----
End of note. Keep iteration shallow and messy; this is a working brain-dump.
